subject: Finalizing closure checklist — Cerulean cost verification & MAP gating
messages:
From: Emily Sharp <emily.sharp@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com; procurement@ceruleanhealth.com
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@ceruleanhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + unit-econ checkpoints before final signatures

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to tighten the MAP so Legal and Procurement can sign off next week. Two quick asks from our side before we lock dates:

1) Tokens / $: can you confirm the expected tokens-per-dollar for our pilot profile (avg prompt 220 tokens, avg completion 430 tokens) and the 95th percentile latency target you’re sizing for?

2) Caching & batching: our infra team wants to understand what assumptions Redwood will make for prefix/KV caching (per-customer warm cache hit rates) and recommended batching parameters for our expected traffic (bursty 5 TPS windows). Any conservative numbers you can share?

3) Evals: we’ll need the eval plan (20 prompts, A/B against baseline) and an evaluation gate that ties to cost sensitivity (if token cost > 12% vs baseline we pause rollout).

We’ve attached the MAP draft with procurement questions inline — hoping we can close by 2025-04-25 if the economics check passes.

Appreciate a compact set of numbers we can share with procurement/legal.

Best,
Emily
Director of Product, Cerulean Health

[Attachment: cerulean_map_draft_v3.pdf (210 KB)]

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sharp <emily.sharp@ceruleanhealth.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + unit-econ checkpoints before final signatures

Emily — thanks for the clear asks. Summary below (keeping it tight for procurement/legal). Attaching a worked workbook with the math.

1) Tokens / $ (pilot profile) — conservative baseline we use for contract sizing: 650 tokens per request (prompt+completion). With Redwood Hosted pricing and expected util for the pilot, that maps to ~3,100 tokens/$ (i.e., ~$0.00032 per token equivalent). That number assumes standard fp16 non-quantized throughput.

2) Latency sizing — we size to P95 < 450ms for the pilot profile with dedicated pooling. If you need tighter SLOs we can provide a higher-tier SLA with a pricing delta.

3) Caching & batching assumptions — conservative defaults we recommend in the MAP:
   - Warm KV/prefix cache hit rate: 25% for initial pilot (assumes cold-start and limited session reuse).
   - Target warm-state hit rate after steady-state: 60% (6-8 weeks of pilot with sticky sessions).
   - Batching: recommend target batch window 25ms for latency-sensitive routes (typical throughput 5 TPS) and 100ms for background inference (higher throughput).

4) Cost sensitivity gating & evals — we’ll provide the eval harness and a runbook. Per your gate: if tokens-per-$ degrades by >12% vs baseline within A/B, we trigger a canary rollback.

Next steps / asks from Cerulean:
 - Confirm whether you want us to size for optimistic (60% steady-state cache) or conservative (25% initial) in the SOW.
 - Procurement: request preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether you need a committed instance.

Attaching token_econ_workbook.xlsx with line-item math + scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic). I’ll loop Neha for any infra details.

Thanks — Diego
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: token_econ_workbook.xlsx (48 KB)]

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com; emily.sharp@ceruleanhealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + unit-econ checkpoints before final signatures

Quick technical clarifications from infra — Emily, copying the assumptions you flagged so procurement has the detail:

- KV/prefix cache sizing: our conservative guidance assumes a per-customer in-memory KV store sized to hold ~1.5x the average active session keyset. For Cerulean’s expected session profile that maps to ~1.6 GB of KV RAM. That supports the warm-state hit rates Diego quoted.
- Cache eviction behavior: LRU with session affinity recommended; cross-shard warm-up takes ~15–30 minutes under steady request mix.
- Batching behavior for 5 TPS burst windows: if you set the target batch window at 25ms we expect batching to add ~5–12ms median overhead but preserve P95 within the 450ms target. If you move to 100ms batching, throughput efficiency improves (~12–18% lower cost) but P95 may increase by ~40–60ms depending on completion length.

If procurement wants conservative contractual numbers, we can use the conservative hit rate and conservative batching (assume no warm cache) and build a quarterly reconciliation clause for realized unit economics.

-Neha
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sharp <emily.sharp@ceruleanhealth.com>; procurement@ceruleanhealth.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com; tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + unit-econ checkpoints before final signatures

Emily / Procurement team — following up with final recommended language to include in the MAP / SOW:

1) Unit economics baseline: parties agree to initial pricing cadence based on conservative estimate (3,100 tokens/$) with monthly reconciliation against actual usage. If realized tokens-per-$ is better than baseline, credits apply to the next invoice; if worse by >12% for two consecutive months, Redwood will execute the rollback/fallback described in the MAP and provide a remediation plan.

2) Caching & batching gating: SOW will specify conservative cache hit rate (25%) for first 30 days. After 30 days, an operations review will assess warm-cache attainment; if warm-cache >=50% we will apply the optimistic price schedule and a credit for prior usage.

3) Eval gate: Redwood to run A/B evaluation (20 prompts) during canary with pass/fail thresholds tied to quality and cost. Failure on cost side (>12% token cost delta) triggers pause.

Action owner & next steps:
 - Cerulean: confirm preferred billing cadence and whether you want a committed instance. (Emily)
 - Redwood: we’ll send an SOW including the conservative numbers above and the reconciliation clause by EOD Tue 2025-04-22. (Diego)
 - Ops: Neha to provide cache sizing appendix and expected warm-up timeline. (Neha)

If procurement wants, Ben will join vendor terms call tomorrow to walk through the reconciliation language.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Diego
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
